rv.q: Perhaps even more surprising is that, somehow, they pull it off.
“Masquerade” has transformed what was formerly regarded as a corny tourist attraction into one of the hottest tickets in New York.
There’s only so much you can “elevate” about a work that fundamentally wants to revel in some schlocky mud.

That’s something new, although the show, which I thought a tad too long, also wants to deliver at those signature Lloyd Webber ditties and thus the result falls uneasily between a new narrative and a new way of telling an old story for the faithful.
This “Masquerade” is silly, frustrating, ethically dubious and frankly thrilling.
This reconfigured Phantom may be closer to a ride than high art, but it sure gives you a closeup look at a lot of terrific craft.
This entire revitalized gothic romance with its 1980s guitar riffs has that invigorating effect.
Even if it’s not remotely scary, Masquerade is inexhaustibly cool.
From here on, Masquerade evolves from a merely fascinating immersive experience to full-on fan service in the most thrilling way possible.
The approach that director Diane Paulus et al take in this intricate, intimate, interactive new production could well appeal to audiences who have never seen Phantom.
While Masquerade offers a memorable adventure in the milieu of Phantom, it’s harder to be moved by Christine’s story when you’re the one doing most of the moving.
Ultimately, it’s the intimacy of the environment that makes Masquerade such a special experience.

What results is not unlike an expensive, exclusive party in a carnival funhouse. While the original “Phantom” was derided by its detractors as a cheesy theme park attraction, “Masquerade” truly is a glorified one.
But Paulus and team have pulled off something miraculous: an immersive evening that retains the essence and dramatic arc of its source material.

The result of this world creation is a truly moving, unforgettable experience that takes you to the darkest depths of the human mind; yet it still provides hope for a brighter future filled with music and light.
